findings.title: Adversarial prize semantics can defeat economic delivery while NFT-outcome proceeds are payable
findings.severity: High under the explicit untrusted-prize DESIGN scope; trust limitation under the narrower honest-prize interface scope
required_capabilities: Sponsor selects or controls a prize contract that can fabricate ERC165/ownership responses or later reject/seize/pause outgoing transfers.
Victims buy entries sufficient to meet reserve; normal trusted quote token and timely authenticated VRF callback; no quote-token, wrapper or victim-wallet compromise required.
sequence: Create with a contract that passes the exact configured receipt and reported-ownership checks.
Sell entries, resolve NftWon and permissionlessly settle the valid winning range.
Fabrication variant: token reports winner ownership without honoring the intended ownership/transfer semantics; prize redemption and sponsor release can both appear successful.
Refusal variant: release sponsor proceeds in an earlier transaction, then every NFT redemption reverts. That local rollback cannot recover already paid proceeds; NftWon has no refund transition.
findings.impact: Sponsor can retain 95% of gross sales while an entrant has no enforceable promised NFT delivery. Quote liabilities can remain perfectly conserved: this is a cross-asset economic guarantee/trust gap, not demonstrated quote-ledger insolvency. No other raffle is drained.
exclusions: Not an exploit against an honest, continuously transferable ERC721 with truthful ownership semantics.
The sealed mock uses a separate actualOwner ledger to illustrate dishonest reports; it is not proof of a particular deployed collection or external market value.
The permanently reverting-prize ordering is source-derived here; no new freeze-token execution campaign was run.

proof.detail: Lines 73-103 define fake semantics; 142-164 demonstrate creation; 167-192 demonstrate buyer payment, fabricated delivery and 95% sponsor payment.
Both tests PASS; adjacent exit code is 0; hashes bound by sealed-artifacts.sha256.
H-1 through H-4 are explicit function fragments of one chain, not four independent High root causes.

remediation_direction: Resolve and consistently state whether adversarial prize semantics are actually supported; no owner acceptance or scope relaxation is inferred.
If restricting assets, validate trusted implementations and their upgrade/pause/seizure authority; ERC165 and self-reported ownerOf cannot establish honesty.

Holding both sponsor and treasury proceeds until delivery plus a bounded refund policy can address refusal, but cannot authenticate a lying token; it also changes winner-dependent liveness and requires a complete policy review.
re_audit_property: Under the chosen supported prize model, entrants cannot lose the retained gross pot without enforceable prize delivery or the specified bounded refund alternative.
Test fabricated receipt/ownerOf, post-escrow pause/seizure, permanent transfer revert, winner refusal, sponsor-before-winner ordering and rollback across separate transactions.
A fix must not claim generic economic authenticity from ownerOf alone.
model_disagreements: DAYBREAK-SIMAO assigns four High function-level entries; merged here as one economic chain while preserving all IDs.
DAYBREAK-GEBAL rates High; SUP-S1 calls conditional High; SUP-A2 calls conditional Medium; OPENAI-PASHOV/TOB/GEBAL and SUP-A1 retain leads or trust gaps.

Absence of a hostile NFT in production source is not a refutation when adversarial prizes are in DESIGN scope; the sealed mock supplies concrete self-report behavior. Conversely, reviewer agreement does not broaden the honest-prize guarantee.

Simao attempt-03 gives five High findings across admission, creation, settlement, redemption and proceeds; this register preserves H-1..H-5 and J IDs but merges the conditional root chain. Claude TIA-1/S6-3 and Gemini FP-M-02 call it Medium; Claude SUP-03 calls it Low integration risk and explicitly not a code defect. No owner acceptance is inferred from that scope interpretation.

findings.title: Temporal and factory-local destination screening permits sponsor-selected clone sinks
required_capabilities: Sponsor deliberately or mistakenly chooses the predictable address of a future clone as immutable sponsorRecipient before it is deployed/registered.
A later successful creation deploys that clone with another configured prize before the first prize release.
Foreign-factory variant additionally needs another deployment and an authorized sponsor/deployer/owner selecting or approving its clone.
sequence: Create A with sponsorRecipient set to future B; B is code-free and not in the registry.
Create B with token ID 2 and verify B equals the predicted address and is now registered.
Cancel empty A into Refunding and release A token ID 1 through unsafe transferFrom; ownerOf==B passes.
Complete B normally: it releases only configured token ID 2; unrelated token ID 1 stays at B, with no generic execution/rescue route.
findings.impact: An honest NFT selected by the sponsor is stranded and the literal no-inter-clone movement promise is violated. A now-known B also makes a sponsor quote release revert and preserve its immutable liability. Foreign-factory quote donations/recipient payouts can become unaccounted holdings; cross-factory ticket-as-prize composition is a scope violation but not necessarily permanent loss.
exclusions: No attacker can transform an arbitrary existing victim EOA into a chosen clone.
No theft of another raffle’s quote balance, winner manipulation, or reduction of buyer refund liability is established.
Only the same-factory empty-refund honest-NFT path was executed in recipient-validation; foreign-factory and quote-lock variants remain source-established, separately scoped.

Counterfactual address predictability alone does not authorize an attacker to select another user’s recipient. CREATE2 or prevrandao address changes are not complete destination-safety or claim-recovery remedies.

proof.detail: Lines 20-32 predict B, configure A, deploy B, transfer token1 into B, then show B releases only token2.
testConfiguredFutureCloneRecipientCanStrandSponsorsOwnPrize PASS; one test; exit 0; integrity checks clean.

remediation_direction: Repeat current destination screening at sponsor-prize delivery to prevent actual known-clone transfer.

A runtime rejection alone does not make an immutable bad recipient claim recoverable; define supported recipients or separately design authenticated redirection without gifting arbitrary callers destination control.
State whether isolation is same-factory or global; a local registry cannot recognize every foreign deployment or future address.
re_audit_property: An address accepted before code deployment cannot later receive a sponsor prize if it is then a prohibited protocol destination.

Regression must use honest ERC721, a real future clone, different configured token IDs, and normal completion of the receiving clone; prove claims remain backed on rejection and document any recovery semantics.
model_disagreements: SUP-A1 calls Informational; SUP-A2 and OPENAI-GEBAL attempt01 call Low; OPENAI-GEBAL attempt02 and DAYBREAK-SIMAO retain self-loss leads.
DAYBREAK-GEBAL and DAYBREAK-TOB emphasize foreign-factory scope. The honest same-factory execution removes that interpretation prerequisite for the temporal variant.

Simao attempt-03 J-4 rejects due sponsor self-harm; Gemini FP-M-01 calls the grouped predictable-address issue Medium; Claude SUP-01 calls sponsor own-loss Low. This register retains source-confirmed Low destination invariant defect with strict own-recipient loss. Gemini NFT-winner delivery into another clone is not established: the clone owning the ticket cannot call owner-only redeemWinningTicket. Sponsor return is actually reproduced independently.

findings.title: Quote issuer sender freeze can block all exits while preserving liabilities
findings.severity: Informational dependency risk; original Medium retained in attribution
required_capabilities: Configured quote token exercises a sender-wide transfer restriction against the raffle, or otherwise reverts its transfers. No canonical deployment/admin state was supplied.
sequence: Issuer/dependency blocks raffle sender after deposits.
Every quote transfer reverts; EVM rollback preserves burns, claim balances and other transaction-local state.
findings.impact: All quote claimants can be temporarily or indefinitely unable to withdraw; transferability of tickets cannot change the frozen sender.
exclusions: No arbitrary participant capability to trigger issuer action demonstrated.
No source-only claim that a deployed USDC instance is currently frozen or that a rescue function can transfer from a blocked sender.
remediation_direction: Document issuer availability and remediation dependencies; an onchain redirect cannot overcome a sender blacklist. Changing quote asset or administrative recovery architecture is a policy change requiring separate review.
re_audit_property: Injected token transfer refusal must preserve every liability and ticket; restoring transfer capability must restore exits. Distinguish fully backed claims from executable liquidity.
model_disagreements: DAYBREAK-SIMAO M-1 assigns Medium; supplemental and OpenAI reports treat this as canonical-dependency availability, not a newly demonstrated authorization/accounting flaw.

findings.title: Fixed sponsor or treasury recipient can lose quote-transfer availability
findings.severity: Informational integration limitation; original Medium retained in attribution
required_capabilities: Issuer freezes a fixed payout recipient after configuration, or that recipient becomes otherwise disallowed.
sequence: Settlement creates the backed fixed-address claim.
Release fails against the same immutable recipient on every retry; other independently payable recipients can still exit if unaffected.
findings.impact: Affected sponsor/treasury claim remains backed but unavailable. This differs from freezing the raffle sender and from theft.
exclusions: No current issuer action established; no owner acceptance inferred.
Bearer ticket owners may transfer their ticket if they retain an executable transfer route; fixed proceeds recipients have no equivalent path.
remediation_direction: If recovery is desired, separately design recipient-authorized redirection, authenticate original entitlement and retain sink checks. Account for the stated no-mutable-configuration goal.
re_audit_property: One blocked fixed recipient must not block sibling claims; authorized recovery must not let an outsider redirect balances.
model_disagreements: DAYBREAK-SIMAO M-2 assigns Medium; other reports retain an immutable-recipient availability limitation.

findings.title: Nominal quote accounting assumes canonical fee-free non-rebasing transfers
required_capabilities: Factory deployer configures an unsupported fee/rebase/false-success token or dependency semantics later depart from the declared canonical behavior.
sequence: Token returns success while transferring fewer units than nominal purchase or payout.
Ledger records nominal units without balance-delta reconciliation.
findings.impact: Unsupported token semantics can underfund liabilities or fake delivery; metadata and six decimals do not prove canonical identity.
exclusions: Quote token is explicitly trusted canonical in DESIGN; this is not attacker-selectable per raffle.
remediation_direction: Verify deployed canonical dependency identity and supported semantics; expanding token support requires deliberate accounting design and adversarial-token tests.
re_audit_property: Supported quote tokens must move exact nominal units; unsupported token tests must be identified as compatibility experiments, not claimed canonical vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Receiver acceptance and address-level ownership do not prove bearer claim usability
required_capabilities: Payer/owner/approved operator selects a receiver that accepts the ticket or NFT but cannot later issue the required claim/transfer call; includes inaccessible future or foreign addresses.
sequence: Safe mint/transfer succeeds or unsafe prize delivery establishes address-level ownership.
Recipient has no usable calling route to exercise the bearer right.
findings.impact: Owner-selected claim can be inaccessible despite intact accounting. General last-actor-exit claims require a capable recipient assumption.
exclusions: No involuntary loss of a normal EOA established.
A receiver hook acceptance is not a promise of arbitrary future call functionality; runtime sink checks cannot classify every arbitrary contract.
remediation_direction: Document capability requirements; enforce known sink checks; if alternate payout is desired, authenticate current bearer ownership and avoid arbitrary caller routing.
re_audit_property: Current owner, former owner, operator and incapable receivers must be distinguished; accounting solvency must not be equated with universal claim usability.

original_attributions.original_label: Safe receipt does not prove exercisable bearer claim

findings.title: Unsolicited assets have no rescue and are outside recorded liabilities
required_capabilities: A sender donates quote tokens, forces native currency, or unsafely transfers an unrelated NFT to the raffle.
sequence: Asset custody increases without a protocol purchase, allocation or configured prize transition.
No general rescue/execution method exists; only configured claims/prize can exit.
findings.impact: Donated assets can be irretrievable. They do not create a liability to the donor, authorize a drain, or make existing claims insolvent under trusted token semantics.
exclusions: Do not count raw custody as owed liability. A donation can make actual quote balance exceed accounted liabilities; equality is valid only in a no-donation model.
Counterfactual sponsor-prize delivery in RF-002 is a protocol-directed transfer and is not dismissed as an unsolicited donation.
remediation_direction: Explicitly document no-rescue behavior and scope accounting invariants. A rescue authority would change the immutability/authority model and must not sweep recorded claims.
re_audit_property: Assert balance >= liabilities under donation scenarios; prove all legitimate claims remain payable and unrelated donations cannot modify settlement or ownership rights.

findings.title: VRF modulo reduction has negligible finite-word bias
required_capabilities: Would require exploiting bias in a trusted uniform 256-bit random word while totalEntries<=2^128-1.
sequence: Modulo maps outputs to 1..totalEntries with at most one-preimage frequency difference.
findings.impact: Statistical bias exists but total variation is below 2^-130 for the stated bounds; no participant-selectable authentic VRF word or practical advantage is shown.
exclusions: Not an exact-uniformity proof; not counted as a security finding.
remediation_direction: Retain explicit randomness assumptions; no complex redesign recommended solely for this negligible bound.
re_audit_property: Selection must remain in sold range and authenticated; quantify bias rather than claim perfect uniformity.

required_capabilities: A buyer trusts an unconfirmed deployment address.
A chain reorganization or equivalent reordered deployment changes which raffle occupies that address; pending approval/purchase remains executable.
sequence: Buyer prepares purchase for unconfirmed address.
Deployment ordering changes before canonical confirmation.
Purchase executes against different configuration at the same address.
findings.impact: Potential purchase against unintended prize/sponsor, contingent on chain/finality and client behavior absent from this source review.

proof.detail: No new execution or formal proof campaign; incoming execution claims remain attributed.

remediation_direction: Wait for deployment confirmation and bind purchase intent to expected immutable configuration or its hash if this risk is in product scope.
re_audit_property: Reproduce on the actual client/chain transaction pipeline before promotion; demonstrate buyer signature executes against altered configuration.

findings.title: An economically unreachable reserve intentionally forces cash outcomes
required_capabilities: Sponsor chooses a positive uint128 reserve above attainable quote-funded entries.
sequence: Create high reserve.
Normal nonempty draw cannot reach reserve and resolves CashWon.
findings.impact: Buyers receive configured cash-branch economics; no promise of feasible NFT threshold is enforced beyond nonzero reserve.

proof.detail: No new execution or formal proof campaign; incoming execution claims remain attributed.

remediation_direction: Display reserve and branch economics prominently; optionally constrain product inputs after economic requirements are agreed.
re_audit_property: Extreme reserve remains arithmetic-safe and resolves CashWon with the exact 80/15/5 allocation.

findings.title: Draw completion depends on a caller paying native VRF fees
required_capabilities: No actor is willing/able to pay the wrapper fee before draw deadline.
sequence: Sales close.
No draw request succeeds or no callback arrives.
Documented request/callback deadline permits refunds.
findings.impact: Possible refund rather than draw; not indefinite custody lock under functioning quote token. Fixed callback gas may overcharge relative to minimal mocks but requires real-wrapper measurement.

proof.detail: No new execution or formal proof campaign; incoming execution claims remain attributed.

remediation_direction: Specify keeper/user fee incentives, quote transaction gas price correctly, and verify native-wrapper configuration and callback gas under actual deployment.
re_audit_property: No caller, exact request deadline, insufficient fee, excess refund rejection and wrapper outage all preserve bounded user exits and atomicity.

assurance_issues.title: Swallowed reverts permit an entirely inactive invariant campaign
assurance_issues.confidence: high for demonstrated experiment; bounded reachability limits retained
assurance_issues.detail: All 9 invariants survived a valid-purchase-always-reverts mutant at 64 runs/depth64; audit_strict 16/depth64 also passed with zero handler reverts. Unit/fuzz/security selection killed it with59 failures. RaffleHandler.sol:61-72 catches purchase failures; many actions silently return; no minimum meaningful activity is proved.
assurance_issues.capabilities: Test harness controls generated actions, callers, time and caught exceptions; no deployed attacker claim.
assurance_issues.remedy: Track independent attempted/successful/unexpected-failure counters; assert allowed actions succeed; seed terminal branches without requiring every random sequence to hit all branches.
assurance_issues.re_audit_property: A contract that rejects all valid purchases must fail a stateful campaign; successful cash/NFT/refund settlement and final exits must have measured witnesses.

assurance_issues.title: Owner-only handler calls mask authorization mutations
assurance_issues.confidence: high for demonstrated experiment; bounded reachability limits retained
assurance_issues.detail: The stateful handler pranks owner for redemption/refunds (RaffleHandler.sol:187-188,207-208), so removing winner owner guard survived all9 bounded invariants. Existing deterministic/fuzz/security tests killed it with3 failures. Two holder addresses do not provide adversarial caller coverage.
assurance_issues.capabilities: Test harness controls generated actions, callers, time and caught exceptions; no deployed attacker claim.
assurance_issues.remedy: Generate outsider, former owner, approved operator, buyer and recipient independently; retain positive current-owner actions.
assurance_issues.re_audit_property: Unauthorized claim attempts must fail with complete state rollback; current bearer must still succeed.

assurance_issues.title: Deadline action prefilters hide rejection-boundary defects
assurance_issues.confidence: high for demonstrated experiment; bounded reachability limits retained
assurance_issues.detail: Handler requestDraw prefilter at RaffleHandler.sol:115-126 and Echidna:67-75 never calls outside the valid window. >= to > mutation survived9 bounded invariants; deterministic selection killed it with3 failures.
assurance_issues.capabilities: Test harness controls generated actions, callers, time and caught exceptions; no deployed attacker claim.
assurance_issues.remedy: Add invalid-action probes at boundary-1, boundary and boundary+1, with independently expected results.
assurance_issues.re_audit_property: At exact request deadline requestDraw must reject and refunds become eligible; invalid calls must reach production rather than no-op in the handler.

assurance_issues.title: Economic oracle is useful but short-run reachability and some ghosts are weak
assurance_issues.confidence: high for demonstrated experiment; bounded reachability limits retained
assurance_issues.detail: Fee500->400bps survived64-run invariants but was killed at run120 in a512-run campaign and by9 unit/fuzz/security failures. Guided existing-oracle probe also killed it. Rate literals are independent; gross/payout ghosts partly copy contract getters/returns. Echidna actor/split gaps are source-reviewed, not mutation-tested.
assurance_issues.capabilities: Test harness controls generated actions, callers, time and caught exceptions; no deployed attacker claim.
assurance_issues.remedy: Seed lifecycle states, count successful branches, measure token balance deltas independently and add exact per-beneficiary Echidna split checks.
assurance_issues.re_audit_property: Wrong fee allocation must be reached and rejected in each outcome; totals alone must not substitute for correct recipient shares.

assurance_issues.title: Python reference model does not restore lazy settlement after unauthorized redemption
assurance_issues.confidence: high for demonstrated experiment; bounded reachability limits retained
assurance_issues.detail: current_protocol_model.py:166-177 mutates through settle_winner:155-163 before raising not-owner. Probe changed settlement_complete false->true, unsettled1e6->0 and sponsor/treasury/winner claims0->150k/50k/800k despite rejection. Solidity transaction rollback and the passing owner/operator unit test preserve state; this is not a production rollback defect.
assurance_issues.capabilities: Test harness controls generated actions, callers, time and caught exceptions; no deployed attacker claim.
assurance_issues.remedy: Prevalidate or snapshot/restore modeled transactions; add full-state rollback comparison and actual differential contract execution if claiming differential assurance.
assurance_issues.re_audit_property: Every rejected modeled action must leave the entire state unchanged just as Solidity does.

assurance_issues.capabilities: Test harness controls generated actions, callers, time and caught exceptions; no deployed attacker claim.
assurance_issues.remedy: Validate exact current-source applicability first, retain full logs/diffs and classify compiler failure/tool failure/timeout separately from assertion kill.
assurance_issues.re_audit_property: Every claimed valid mutant must compile and have a documented semantic change; mutation score denominator must exclude invalid definitions.

remediation_order.action: Resolve the promised prize guarantee and scope conflict before any fix. Choose enforceable supported collection semantics/trust policy or a specified funded failure fallback. Retain all money required for any refund, including the 5% protocol leg. Gating sponsor payout alone cannot make an arbitrary lying ownerOf truthful.
remediation_order.re_audit: Fake callback/ownerOf, paused or revoked custody after genuine escrow, independent payout ordering, timeout/fallback, every claim permutation, atomic rollback and no cross-raffle loss.

remediation_order.action: Make outbound NFT destination policy explicit and consistent at transfer time; runtime refusal prevents cross-clone movement but does not restore an immutable stranded claim. Specify any recovery authority separately. Validate treasury and recipient custody at deployment and creation.
remediation_order.re_audit: Honest ERC721 future-clone sponsor return; own/same/foreign factory sinks; counterfactual ticket custody; recipient becomes unusable; existing liabilities and unrelated claims remain safe.

remediation_order.action: Improve handler success reachability, adversarial callers, exact boundary attempts and independent reference rollback; repair stale mutation targets and run meaningful positive and negative transitions.
remediation_order.re_audit: All four valid temporary mutants must be killed by intended properties at recorded bounds; compare success/revert/no-op action counts and branch/actor coverage. Python unauthorized lazy redemption must roll back as Solidity does.

remediation_order.action: Integrate canonical claim-aware UX, robust log indexing, confirmed deployment binding, marketplace pending-randomness policy and actual-chain dependency/fee checks.
